boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Stonehill College
boards.description: Ten named Stonehill destinations with published evening or overnight access details, spanning food, study, reflection, and campus activity.

cards.title: The Hill
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College dining venue
cards.notes: Check the published schedule before heading over; the venue lists service through 11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining stop with the latest listed food hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill lists The Hill open 6 p.m.–11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 6 p.m.–1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Published dining schedule lists service until 11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday; verify schedule changes before visiting.

cards.title: Ace's Place
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College dining venue
cards.notes: Use the current dining schedule for timing; Ace's Place lists midnight closing Monday–Thursday and Sunday, with earlier weekend hours.
cards.short_summary: A named dining venue with several midnight-closing nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill lists Ace's Place open until midnight Monday–Thursday and Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Published dining schedule lists midnight closing Monday–Thursday and Sunday; Friday closes at 9 p.m. and Saturday at 6 p.m.

cards.title: Roche Dining Commons
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College campus dining building
cards.notes: Plan around the building schedule, which lists closing at 11 p.m. on several nights and 1 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining building with published late building hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill Operations lists Roche Dining Commons open until 1 a.m. on Friday and Saturday and until 11 p.m. on Monday–Thursday and Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Published building schedule lists 1 a.m. closing Friday and Saturday; food-service availability may differ from building access.

cards.title: College Center
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College campus building
cards.notes: Use this named campus destination when a late indoor stop is needed; the Operations schedule lists the College Center open 24 hours.
cards.short_summary: A College Center building listed as open around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill Operations lists the College Center open 24 hours on weekdays and weekends.
cards.access_notes: The official schedule lists the building open 24 hours and notes the front door is unlocked for computer-lab access; observe posted access rules.

cards.title: MacPhaidin Library
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College library
cards.notes: Bring what you need for a focused stop; the Operations schedule lists midnight closing Monday–Thursday and Sunday, with card access noted.
cards.short_summary: A library destination with several published midnight closings.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill Operations lists MacPhaidin Library closing at midnight Monday–Thursday and Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Published schedule lists midnight closing Monday–Thursday and Sunday and card access via the south/east corner entrance; check access eligibility.

cards.title: Madigan Carriage House
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College campus building
cards.notes: Use the named Carriage House only within its normal campus rules; Stonehill's Operations page lists it open 24 hours on weekdays and weekends.
cards.short_summary: A campus building listed as open 24 hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill Operations lists Madigan Carriage House open 24 hours on weekdays and weekends.
cards.access_notes: The official building schedule lists 24-hour weekday and weekend access and no card-access requirement; follow any posted campus restrictions.

cards.title: Meehan School of Business
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College academic building
cards.notes: For a late study-oriented destination, use the School's listed 24-hour areas rather than assuming all rooms are available after the main building closes.
cards.short_summary: An academic building with specified 24-hour study-related areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill Operations lists 24-hour access for the Meehan School of Business computer lab, Capital Markets Room, Great Room, Collaboration Zone, study spaces, and reading rooms.
cards.access_notes: The building lists a 10 p.m. close, while specified study-related spaces are listed for 24-hour access; use only spaces for which you have access.

cards.title: Shields Science Center
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College science building
cards.notes: Head specifically to the Pettit Atrium for late access; Stonehill lists the atrium as open 24 hours while some lab access is restricted.
cards.short_summary: A science-building destination with a 24-hour named atrium.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill Operations states that the Pettit Atrium in Shields Science Center is open 24 hours.
cards.access_notes: Pettit Atrium is listed open 24 hours; the page says some science students have lab access, so do not assume access to laboratories.

cards.title: Duffy Academic Center
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College academic building
cards.notes: Use this named academic building for an evening stop before its listed 11 p.m. close, and rely on the posted access route if eligible.
cards.short_summary: An academic destination with 11 p.m. listed closing times.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill Operations lists Duffy Academic Center open until 11 p.m. on weekdays and weekends.
cards.access_notes: Published schedule lists 11 p.m. weekday and weekend closing, with north/east entrance card access for people with clearance.

cards.title: Chapel of Mary
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College chapel
cards.notes: For a quiet late-evening destination, visit before the published 11 p.m. close and follow any event, worship, or building-use notices in place.
cards.short_summary: A chapel listed as open through 11 p.m. every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill Operations lists the Chapel of Mary open 7 a.m.–11 p.m. on weekdays and weekends.
cards.access_notes: Published building schedule lists 11 p.m. closing on weekdays and weekends with no card-access requirement; respect chapel programming and posted rules.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time on campus or nearby in Easton.

cards.title: Walk Stonehill’s marked trails
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College campus, Easton
cards.notes: Choose a designated, marked trail and take a low-key walk together; remain on public trail areas and follow posted campus guidance.
cards.short_summary: A campus walk on trails Stonehill identifies as public space.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill’s campus-access memorandum lists designated, marked walking trails as public spaces open to the general public without special authorization.
cards.access_notes: Use only designated, marked trails; the College may restrict access for safety or operations.

cards.title: Meet at MacPháidín Library
cards.subtitle: Public areas, Stonehill College campus
cards.notes: Bring a book or conversation and use the public areas; visitors should register at The Desk each time they visit.
cards.short_summary: A campus library stop with designated public areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill identifies MacPháidín Library’s public areas as open to the general public without special authorization; its library page says visitors are welcome except during three weeks at each semester’s end.
cards.access_notes: Visitors must register at The Desk; access excludes the three weeks at the end of each semester.

cards.title: Browse the public archives area
cards.subtitle: Martin Institute Archives, Stonehill College
cards.notes: Visit the public research area to explore campus-history materials; do not enter archival storage or any space closed for a private event.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing archive space for a history-focused hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill’s campus-access memorandum lists the Martin Institute Archives as a public space; it separately says archival storage is private while the public research area remains public unless closed for a private event.
cards.access_notes: Use the public research area only; archival storage is not public.

cards.title: Start at the Welcome Center
cards.subtitle: May Building, Stonehill College campus
cards.notes: Use the public Welcome Center as a meeting point before a campus walk; keep the visit within the designated admission area.
cards.short_summary: A designated public campus arrival point.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill’s campus-access memorandum lists the Welcome Center as a public space open to the general public without special authorization.
cards.access_notes: The rest of May Building outside the Office of Undergraduate Admission area remains private.

cards.title: Claim a free athletic-event ticket
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College athletics venues
cards.notes: Check the current home schedule, then use the student ticket benefit for an alcohol-free game-night outing with friends.
cards.short_summary: Student tickets for Stonehill athletic events are listed as free.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill’s 2026–2027 tuition-and-fees page states that the General Service Fee covers free tickets to Stonehill College athletic events.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Tuition and Fees | Stonehill College
cards.access_notes: For Stonehill students using the included ticket benefit; confirm the event’s current ticket process before going.

cards.title: Join an intramural activity
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College recreation program
cards.notes: Look for a current intramural offering and invite a friend to register with you; participation is included for Stonehill students.
cards.short_summary: Included student access to intramural activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill’s 2026–2027 tuition-and-fees page states that the General Service Fee covers participation in intramural and recreational activities.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Tuition and Fees | Stonehill College
cards.access_notes: For Stonehill students; check current intramural registration and eligibility details.

cards.title: Plan a recreation session
cards.subtitle: Stonehill College recreation facilities
cards.notes: Pick a current recreational activity and go together; Stonehill lists courts, tracks, fields, and trails among its recreation spaces.
cards.short_summary: Student recreational activities with no separate purchase listed.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill’s 2026–2027 tuition-and-fees page states that the General Service Fee covers participation in intramural and recreational activities.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Tuition and Fees | Stonehill College
cards.access_notes: For Stonehill students; use facilities according to current recreation access and scheduling rules.

cards.title: Use the library’s public internet
cards.subtitle: Ames Free Library, 53 Main Street, Easton
cards.notes: Bring a project or shared playlist plan and use the public Wi-Fi; ask the reference desk for a guest pass if you need a computer.
cards.short_summary: Free public internet and guest computer access downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Ames Free Library’s policy says it provides free and open internet access through public computer stations and a public Wi-Fi network, and non-cardholders may request a guest pass.
cards.access_notes: Computer users without an Ames Free Library card may ask the reference librarian for a guest pass.

cards.title: Catch a Queset Garden concert
cards.subtitle: Queset Garden at Ames Free Library, Easton
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or chair for lawn seating and check the weather before heading over; the series welcomes non-alcoholic drinks and snacks.
cards.short_summary: Family-friendly outdoor concerts offered free to everyone.
cards.evidence_claim: Ames Free Library states that its 2026 Queset Garden Concert Series is free and open to all, family-friendly, and held on select Thursdays from June 25 through September 10.
cards.source_title: Queset Garden Concert Series | Ames Free Library
cards.access_notes: Outdoor lawn seating; bring a blanket or chair. Shows may be canceled or rescheduled for inclement weather.

cards.entity_name: Ames Free Library Library of Things
cards.title: Borrow Giant Jenga for a hang
cards.subtitle: Ames Free Library, 53 Main Street, Easton
cards.notes: Check the catalog for Giant Jenga availability, borrow it through the library, and set up a relaxed game session with friends.
cards.short_summary: A borrowable oversized game in the library’s Library of Things.
cards.evidence_claim: Ames Free Library’s Library of Things page lists Giant Jenga as an item available to borrow.
cards.source_title: Library of Things | Ames Free Library
cards.access_notes: Borrowing requires availability and the library’s applicable borrowing access; check the catalog before visiting.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named Stonehill spaces for quiet reading, focused calls, digital work, or collaborative coursework.

cards.title: MacPháidín Library Second Floor
cards.subtitle: MacPháidín Library · quiet zone
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing that benefits from a quiet floor, then settle into one of the seating areas overlooking campus.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-floor option with tucked-away seating and campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill identifies the library’s second floor as a quiet zone with comfortable seating in numerous spots, including some with campus views.
cards.source_title: Hot Spots and Hidden Corners | Stonehill College
cards.access_notes: Located in MacPháidín Library; consult the College’s current building-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: MacPháidín Library Third Floor
cards.subtitle: MacPháidín Library · quiet zone
cards.notes: Head upstairs for a quieter setting and choose a comfortable seat for solo reading, outlining, or sustained laptop work.
cards.short_summary: The library’s upper quiet floor for concentrated individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill identifies the library’s third floor as a quiet zone with comfortable seating in numerous spots, including some with campus views.
cards.source_title: Hot Spots and Hidden Corners | Stonehill College
cards.access_notes: Located in MacPháidín Library; consult the College’s current building-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: MacPháidín Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: MacPháidín Library · reservable individual or group rooms
cards.notes: Reserve a room online for a focused solo block or a small-group session; standard bookings are capped at two hours.
cards.short_summary: Bookable rooms that separate focused work from the library’s first-floor activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill says its library study rooms can be reserved online for individual or group study in two-hour periods.
cards.source_title: Back to School: Resources for Students | Stonehill College
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the library’s online booking system; the College says rooms are booked in two-hour periods.

cards.title: Zoom Room (ML 211)
cards.subtitle: MacPháidín Library second floor · reservable
cards.notes: Reserve ML 211 when you need a professional backdrop for a remote interview, presentation, or online conference.
cards.short_summary: A large reservable library room set up for polished video calls.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill describes ML 211 as a large Zoom Room with an attractive backdrop and directs students to reserve it through the study-room form.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required through the study-room booking form; the room is ML 211 in MacPháidín Library.

cards.title: Digital Innovation Lab (107)
cards.subtitle: MacPháidín Library Digital Hub
cards.notes: Use this named Digital Hub space when coursework calls for technology-supported research or a digital project consultation.
cards.short_summary: A library Digital Hub workspace dedicated to technology use across campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill lists the Digital Innovation Lab, room 107, among MacPháidín Library’s studio spaces for faculty and students.
cards.access_notes: The College lists this as a studio space faculty and students can use; request use through the library as needed.

cards.title: Huddle Hutch (108)
cards.subtitle: MacPháidín Library Digital Hub
cards.notes: Use the Huddle Hutch for a compact project session, then coordinate with the library if you need to arrange access.
cards.short_summary: A specifically named Digital Hub studio space for collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill lists the Huddle Hutch, room 108, among the studio spaces that faculty and students can use in the MacPháidín Library Digital Hub.
cards.access_notes: The College lists this as a studio space faculty and students can use; confirm availability with the library.

cards.title: Podcasting Studio (112)
cards.subtitle: MacPháidín Library Digital Hub
cards.notes: Plan recorded narration, an audio assignment, or a research interview here; arrange the studio through the library beforehand.
cards.short_summary: A named Digital Hub studio for coursework involving recorded audio.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill lists the Podcasting Studio, room 112, among the studio spaces faculty and students can use in the MacPháidín Library Digital Hub.
cards.access_notes: The library provides a dedicated booking link for the Podcasting Studio; arrange use in advance.

cards.title: Great Room
cards.subtitle: Leo J. Meehan School of Business
cards.notes: Choose a table in the large lobby for group planning or independent work, keeping scheduled events in mind.
cards.short_summary: A large Meehan lobby with tables used as a group-project workspace.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill describes the Great Room as a large lobby and says students use tables there as a dynamic workspace for group projects.
cards.source_title: Leo J. Meehan School of Business | Stonehill College
cards.access_notes: The College lists Meehan’s regular building hours separately and notes card access at the east entrance.

cards.title: Collaboration Zone
cards.subtitle: Leo J. Meehan School of Business
cards.notes: Use this dedicated collaboration space to compare drafts, map a project, or work through shared course materials together.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-named collaboration area in the Meehan School of Business.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill lists a Collaboration Zone among the Leo J. Meehan School of Business building features and identifies it as an innovative collaboration space.
cards.source_title: Meehan School of Business | Stonehill College
cards.access_notes: Located in the Leo J. Meehan School of Business; current operations information lists card access at the east entrance.

cards.entity_name: Meehan School of Business Computer Lab
cards.title: Meehan School of Business Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Leo J. Meehan School of Business
cards.notes: Set up here when an assignment needs a campus computer or data tools, and verify which lab seats are available on arrival.
cards.short_summary: A named Meehan computer-work option with listed 24-hour access.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill lists computer labs among Meehan’s building features, and its operations page lists 24-hour access for the building’s Computer Lab.
cards.access_notes: Stonehill lists 24-hour access for the Meehan Computer Lab; card access is listed at the east entrance.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Easton destinations on practical Stonehill-area corridors, each with a direct source for its location or offering.

cards.title: Ames Free Library
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor, North Easton
cards.notes: Use the library’s public hours to plan a focused browse, a reference question, or a quiet stop on the Main Street corridor.
cards.short_summary: A public library stop at 53 Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Ames Free Library lists its address as 53 Main Street, Easton, and publishes public library hours.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours before going; it lists Sunday as closed.

cards.entity_name: Queset House at Ames Free Library
cards.title: Queset House
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor, North Easton
cards.notes: Look for a library program or reserve an eligible meeting space; confirm availability with Ames Free Library before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A library-associated gathering space on Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Ames Free Library’s Queset House rental guide identifies Queset House at 53 Main Street in Easton.
cards.source_title: Queset House at the Ames Free Library — Room Rental Guide
cards.access_notes: Room use and fees depend on group type and timing; contact the library for eligibility.

cards.title: Oakes Ames Memorial Hall
cards.subtitle: Barrows Street corridor, North Easton
cards.notes: Check the hall’s calendar or arrange a tour before visiting; the building and grounds make a clearly identifiable historic stop.
cards.short_summary: A historic public building at 3 Barrows Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies Oakes Ames Memorial Hall in North Easton as an Olmsted-designed public building.
cards.access_notes: Interior access is event- or tour-dependent; verify directly with the hall.

cards.title: The Children's Museum in Easton
cards.subtitle: Sullivan Avenue corridor, North Easton
cards.notes: Plan this hands-on museum for a daytime visit, especially when accompanying younger siblings or visiting family; review admission first.
cards.short_summary: Three floors of interactive exhibits on Sullivan Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum lists its address as 9 Sullivan Avenue and describes three floors of interactive hands-on exhibits.
cards.source_title: The Children's Museum in Easton — Visit
cards.access_notes: Admission is required; consult the museum’s current hours and ticket information.

cards.title: Frothingham Hall
cards.subtitle: Barrows Street corridor, North Easton
cards.notes: Check Easton Recreation’s schedule for a drop-in class or program, then collect any applicable activity materials at the hall.
cards.short_summary: A town recreation-program location at 15 Barrows Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Easton Recreation states that its activity punch-card classes are located at Frothingham Hall, 15 Barrows Street.
cards.source_title: Town of Easton Recreation — Activity Punch Cards
cards.access_notes: Programs and fees vary; verify the current recreation schedule before attending.

cards.title: Easton Community Access Television
cards.subtitle: Oliver Street corridor, North Easton
cards.notes: Explore ECAT’s community programming or ask about volunteering and production instruction at its Oliver Street studio office.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit community-media resource on Oliver Street.
cards.evidence_claim: ECAT lists its office at 50 Oliver Street and says it provides community programming plus production instruction.
cards.access_notes: Contact ECAT before visiting to confirm volunteer or studio opportunities.

cards.title: The Beanery on Washington
cards.subtitle: Washington Street corridor, North Easton
cards.notes: Use this as a named coffee-shop stop on Washington Street; confirm its current menu, hours, and accessibility directly before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A Stonehill-listed coffee-shop destination at 181 Washington Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill College lists The Beanery on Washington at 181 Washington Street, North Easton.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase; verify current operating details with the business.

cards.title: Farmer's Daughter
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor, North Easton
cards.notes: Choose this Main Street restaurant for a meal with visiting family or friends, and verify reservations, menu, and hours directly first.
cards.short_summary: A Stonehill-listed restaurant at 122 Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill College lists Farmer’s Daughter at 122 Main Street in North Easton.
cards.access_notes: Meals require purchase; confirm current service and reservation details with the restaurant.

cards.title: Simpson Spring
cards.subtitle: Washington Street corridor, South Easton
cards.notes: Browse the store’s locally sourced food and pantry selection, or stop in for spring-water products; check current hours before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A family-run spring-water and food store at 719 Washington Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson Spring identifies its store at 719 Washington Street and describes locally sourced food, pantry, and wellness products.
cards.source_title: Simpson Spring Company — Visit Simpson Spring
cards.access_notes: Purchases are optional but products require payment; the business lists weekday and Saturday hours.

cards.title: Borderland State Park
cards.subtitle: Massapoag Avenue corridor, North Easton
cards.notes: Plan a daylight trail, disc-golf, fishing, or mansion-tour outing; choose an activity that matches current weather and park guidance.
cards.short_summary: A state park with trails, a historic mansion, and outdoor activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Massachusetts DCR lists Borderland State Park at 259 Massapoag Avenue and names hiking, biking, fishing, boating, tennis, and disc golf.
cards.access_notes: Parking fees may apply; check DCR’s current hours, conditions, and activity restrictions before visiting.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Stonehill College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend sequence that moves from campus orientation and food to spaces for study, recreation, reflection, and involvement.

cards.title: Start with a meal at The Commons
cards.subtitle: First stop: Stonehill’s primary dining hall
cards.notes: Use your first campus meal to orient yourself: find the dining entrance, review the options, and choose a table that makes meeting a neighbor easy.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a familiar campus gathering point.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill identifies The Commons as its primary dining hall and an all-you-care-to-dine venue.
cards.access_notes: College-run dining venue for students, faculty, staff, and guests of the campus community; meal access or payment may be required.

cards.title: Locate Student Engagement
cards.subtitle: Roche Dining Commons, room 103
cards.notes: Drop by or save the contact details for Student Engagement, then ask how to find current campus programming and first-year involvement opportunities.
cards.short_summary: Set up a reliable route to campus programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill’s Office of Student Engagement is located in Roche Dining Commons, room 103, and focuses on orientation, student organizations, leadership, and campus-wide programming.
cards.access_notes: Contact the office for current programming and visitor guidance.

cards.title: Make MacPháidín Library your study landmark
cards.subtitle: Campus library with Ace’s Place inside
cards.notes: Walk through the library early, pick out a desk or collaborative area you might return to, and note that Ace’s Place is located in the building.
cards.short_summary: Choose a recognizable place for future study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill lists Ace’s Place as a dining venue in MacPháidín Library.
cards.access_notes: Confirm library access and service hours through the library before planning a late visit.

cards.title: Take a break at Ace’s Place
cards.subtitle: Inside MacPháidín Library
cards.notes: If you want a short reset during your library walk, use Ace’s Place for a beverage or to-go item and then continue exploring campus.
cards.short_summary: Pair a library stop with an on-site café.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill states that Ace’s Place, in MacPháidín Library, serves Starbucks beverages, pastries, and to-go items.
cards.access_notes: Retail dining venue; purchases are required for food or beverages.

cards.entity_name: Thomas and Donna May School of Arts & Sciences
cards.title: Find the May School’s blue-marble wall
cards.subtitle: A campus landmark in the May School lobby
cards.notes: Walk through the lobby and look for the blue-marble wall; use the building as a waypoint while you get comfortable navigating academic spaces.
cards.short_summary: Add a distinctive academic building to your mental map.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill says the May School of Arts & Sciences opened in fall 2018 and that its lobby includes a large blue-marble wall.
cards.source_title: Stonehill College from A to Z | Stonehill College
cards.access_notes: Academic building; observe posted building-access guidance.

cards.title: See W.B. Mason Stadium
cards.subtitle: Stonehill field hockey, football, lacrosse, and track & field venue
cards.notes: Add the stadium to your walking loop and check the official athletics schedule later if you want to attend a scheduled, public-facing contest.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented to a major Stonehill athletics landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill identifies W.B. Mason Stadium as home to its field hockey, football, lacrosse, and track and field programs, with seating for 2,400.
cards.source_title: Stonehill College from A to Z | Stonehill College
cards.access_notes: Access depends on scheduled events and facility policies; verify details with Stonehill Athletics.

cards.title: Check out recreational sports options
cards.subtitle: Sports Complex
cards.notes: Browse recreational offerings and choose one low-commitment activity to try once schedules are posted, whether that is intramurals, club sport, or group exercise.
cards.short_summary: Explore structured and casual ways to be active.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill Recreational Sports serves the campus community through sports, fitness, wellness, and recreational activities and is based in the Sports Complex.
cards.access_notes: Participation and facility access vary by activity; consult Recreational Sports for current requirements.

cards.title: Try a Stonehill Quiz Bowl meeting
cards.subtitle: Student-led trivia activity
cards.notes: If trivia appeals, look for the next meeting and attend as a newcomer; the organization describes its sessions as team question play and welcomes all experience levels.
cards.short_summary: Meet people through collaborative campus trivia.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill describes Quiz Bowl as a student-led trivia organization whose meetings involve team question play; all are welcome regardless of experience or commitment.
cards.access_notes: Meeting times and locations change; check the current club listing or contact Student Engagement.

cards.title: Look for an Art Club craft session
cards.subtitle: Also known as Craft Club
cards.notes: Save the club listing, then watch for a session where you can make a project alongside other students; the College says supplies are provided for its crafts.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on way to connect over a shared project.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill’s Art Club, also called Craft Club, makes crafts including canvas paintings and succulent decorating, and its listing says supplies are provided.
cards.access_notes: Check the current club schedule and location before attending.

cards.title: End with a quiet Chapel of Mary visit
cards.subtitle: One of Stonehill’s campus worship spaces
cards.notes: If quiet reflection or worship is part of your weekend, check the campus schedule and visit respectfully; Campus Ministry lists the Chapel of Mary among its worship locations.
cards.short_summary: Close the loop with a reflective campus landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehill states that Masses are celebrated throughout the week in the Chapel of Mary, Chapel of Our Lady of Sorrows, and residence-hall chapels.
cards.access_notes: Worship times and building access vary; consult Campus Ministry’s current information before visiting.
